21 Rio.text: I’ve been dealing with a utility bill dispute since the end of July, and the management has done nothing but lie, stall, and give me the runaround. My final bill showed over 24,000 gallons of water usage in a unit that was completely vacant except for a few brief visits. For comparison, when the unit was fully occupied for an entire month, the usage was only 2,370 gallons. That’s more than 10x higher when nobody was living there, clearly a leak or meter issue.

No window in my bedroom, Usually only 1 elevator is working, elevators always smell bad, no one knows the code for the pool😭

2400 Nueces.text: Quiet, clean, responsive maintenance, super cold A/C, plenty of hot water. Mailroom has odd hours but otherwise perfect.

I have the best living experience of all my other friends in West Campus since the building is maintained and the university doesn't cheap out. 26 West.text: Found online when looking for places near engineering side of campus. Application fee was atrocious and couldn’t get that waived when we signed — should’ve waited. 20 min walk from campus, elevator sometimes doesn’t work so lower floors are recommended.

Legacy on Rio.text: Includes gym, courtyard, rooftop area, vending machines, study spots, and a slide. Elevators are really slow. Maintenance is pretty good though!

Nueces Co-op.text: 500 deposit for parking but you get it back. Not a clean or modern apartment-style place. It kind of looks like a prison, but when you make it your own, it works out. It's the definition of “at least you have a head to rest”. You're required to do two hours of labor in order to live here. Labor includes: taking care of plants, cleaning walkways, cleaning elevators, cleaning the laundry room, etc. The CO-OP has 3 sections, which is why we're called the Super Co-op. The first and second floors are Laurel, the third is Nueces, and the fourth and fifth are Halstead. Nueces is the only section of the building where rooms have their own kitchen, and everyone has their own restroom. All the other floors have a communal kitchen, and as part of their labor, they also have to cook for everyone else, depending on what's on the menu. All of it is student ran so there is drama, but we do report to a main office.

Nueces Corner Condos.text: Older building, 1-beds don’t get in-unit laundry

Rambler Apartments.text: Hidden fees, outrageously expensive parking. Good gym and lobby

Redpoint San Marcos.text: Unreliable bus, developing gym, nice pool and sand volleyball area.

Found through a leasing agent. We checked out a lot of places like The Block and Quarters. My bathroom is attached to my room and there's not too many amenities — a gym and a lobby with some broken games — but we have a roof with a patio! So good for the price

Didn’t have water for two weeks, management is really lazy on compensation, maintenance is very fast and on top of it, elevators are pretty slow on busy hours, lease doesn’t disclose that some rooms are smaller than other and neither does the management tell you

San Gabriel Square.text: 2 months free rent will be 650. There is free parking but there is also the option for reserved parking for $20 a month. No in-unit laundry but there is some in the buildings.

Sparq on Rio.text: Slow front office, amenities are limited.

Found just by browsing Google, no hidden fees. Fine, just a far walk- frat across the street is loud at times

$$ off if you resigned ($100 a month, totaling $1,200)

The Castilian.text: sucks, includes a gym and pretty okay food
elevators are pretty slow and some of the washing/drying machines are kinda scuffed
Elevators are really slow, no kitchen, shared bathroom, includes Meal plan!

The Marian Condominiums.text: Extra fees. Parking included. Dim light. Water not included.

Elevators have been broken for like a month once, the sauna doesn't work, the bowling alley doesn't work, we have a pool, a gym, a hot tub, study rooms, a printer yet the printer never works, and a standing tanning bed.

Torre.text: Close to campus, nice gym and rooftop area with pool

Elevator broken for most of semester; close to campus, pool; newly-renovated lobby and study-area; small gym; friendly management; many broken items, lights, furniture upon arrival that was promptly fixed.

Roach infestation when we moved in, elevator is broken and they are not planning on fixing it bc they are broke, redid entire lobby for no reason (maybe this is where the money went), bitchy management (basically tried to pin the roach issue on us when they knew about it before we moved in and did not tell us)

One time payment of $200 for utilities. Enjoy the single just think the price is a little high

Union on 24th.text: About 4 or 5 working elevators of 8. Pool, gym, dog spa, grills, movie theater, yoga/pilates room, basketball hoop, etc.

When you live under a popular amenity like the basketball court or the boxing gym, the sound from the basketball bouncing or boxing gym music gets SO loud. These amenities are open 10am-10pm, so it's just constant noise all day long and it has disrupted interviews, studying, and sleeping. My mental health has never been worse. My roommates and I have complained to management multiple times, and they'll just brush you off. We didn't know we'd be under the basketball court when we first signed either, we were notified of our room number about a month before we moved in.

Floor 23. It’s nice. The amenities are really nice (Community Study Areas, Private Meeting Areas, Theatre Space, Gaming Space, Basketball Court, Boxing Area, Golf Simulator, Spin Studio, Gym, Makers Space (Art/Crafts), Dog Park, Dog Spa/Wash). Hidden Fees: Rent Service Fee? (It’s like ≈6 a month), another 9% service fee for utilities. Like— the rent is already sky high, wdym you need “service fee”?? Why is it not built in?😭😭😭😭 the rent is enough to cover “services” bruh. I like the Trash Chute, each floor can throw trash easily. Residents aren’t really respectful with it though, not a building problem, it’s a people problem. Wall noise cancellation is good. Front door and window noise cancellation is not, I hear cars screeching to a stop and sirens everyday. The counter/cabinets material is cheap wood, it’s stick wallpaper type sh.

Union on San Antonio.text: Very close to campus, elevators are very quick, had some maintenance issues with room that are taking a while to get fixed, right next to Target

Village at East Riverside.text: Bus commute about 40 minutes and 1 on bad traffic days but actually only about 20 minutes away, pest issues

Villas at San Gabriel.text: Elevators are always broken. Gym, pool, and basketball court amenities. Staff is generally alright, but they increased our rent by over 100 a month for next year so we're moving out.

Villas on 24th.text: They consider themselves a "Luxury" apartment, and while the amenities such as the nice gym, pool area, and basketball court might seem nice. The building is not that great once living here. The noise travel is bad, and you can hear your neighbors next door screaming, crying, or just doing anything. The 1st year they opened their residents were insanely spoiled and such snobs, they don't care about how nice the things they have that they will just destroy them. They'll break down elevators, kick walls, scream into hallways, vomit in elevators because they have too much to drink, break glass into the pool, and just hallways a mess because they know that "someone" will just clean it for them. Security was also an issue the first year, they would stop you if you did not look like the usual residents that were white and wore lululemon and polos. They would first assume you were a door dasher or a cleaning person, and demand that you show your fob. But if you looked like the "usual" resident they wouldn't even ask. Now they ask anyone and everyone for their fob because so many POC were experiencing this same issue. The management team also seem irritated when you have issues with things on their property that should be fixed or cleaned? They also make you pay for a third party delivery service that delivers on their own time, so if you rely on same day shipping, you can't anymore. While the apartment is nice at first and glamorous, once you live here you're going to have issues. But if you are low maintenance, a snob, spoiled, and the casual drunk and screamer at 3am in the hallways, oh and not a POC then you would fit right in!
Close to campus, has nice amenities, security at night, new!, elevator issues, loud and messy residents but complex cleans up their messes fast! But thin walls…
Pretty clean most of the time but it can get dirty bc of the frat and sorority people. Haven't had any issues maintenance or management wise though

Villas on 26th.text: Tight parking garage and small amenities not worth using in my opinion.
UT Realtor we had a $80 amenity fee once we first moved in. Things break here a lot; maintenance is good but annoying putting in a request weekly
Wanted to just sign with friends near the engineering area. There is a pretty bad cockroach problem so we have to kill them every day

Villas on Guadalupe.text: Close to campus, two gyms and two pools, also a rooftop area
All gates and doors use the app Geo Key, which can be sketchy and locks you out if your phone dies
Sister complex to venue on guad so we have access to both building's amenities. This is also for a larger room and furnished so $100 extra in the base rent. (Originally 1122)

Villas on Nueces.text: Slow elevators, Loud garbage truck noises at night, small gym. Although it is close to campus and they give you a massive TV and apple TV.
Close to campus. Broken elevators. Hidden fees. Low quality maintenance. Small building. Big rooms

Villas on Rio.text: Walls are thin but amenities are great. It's a greek life apartment so expect it to be loud at nights. Apartment lobby and halls get cleaned daily. Maintenance is slow and there are only 3 elevators for 19 floors. Front desk people are helpful. Deliveries rarely get stolen. If you live next to the trash chute then it smells terrible and overflows on weekends. I live in a 2x2 and have the room with no window, but the large layout and space makes up for it.

So many hidden premium fees, elevators ALWAYS broken, the parking garage has been broken for months, the pool is closed at least 3x a month, managers are always gone and never helpful. Only nice thing is that the maintenance guys are so sweet and work very hard to fix everything, there just are way too many people and issues for the 3 of them.

Scoured around the internet! No hidden fees (just read the contract carefully). I really like my experience overall. Only downside is that mold grows and in one particular bathroom, it’s genuinely horrible (the smell, how fast mold grows, etc)

Waterford Condominiums.text: Parking is included. The garage ceiling tiles are kind of falling off. Maintenance is nonexistent, but the price makes it worth it

West Campus Elloras.text: Things break often and management is slow unless the issue is urgent (like a pipe leak)

West Campus Flats.text: Community laundry, decently cozy but definitely not a new building. Surrounded by frats and co-ops.

Windtree Condominiums.text: I like having my own bathroom, it's also just a 5 min walk from the CPE

Yugo Austin Corner.text: No amenities, far from campus but right next to bus stop, and rooms are huge
Hidden fees, water & electricity are not included, VERY few amenities

Decent apartment. The only downside to living here was in the fall semester when the elevator would go out all the time and we lived on the top floor. They have gotten a new contractor who seems to have really turned things around elevator-wise. It may seem far from campus but the bus stop is right outside your door. Doesn't have a gym or dedicated study rooms (only a little area in the lobby) and I know there are places that go for around the same rate with gyms. Also really nice if you're a cyclist because they have a dedicated bike cage in the parking garage. Plus if you're a dog owner they have their own closed off dog park in the back.

Yugo Austin Rio.text: Includes gym, was given the wrong room on move in, a couple WiFi problems, broken dishwasher, faulty kitchen outlets
Close to campus, elevators sometimes malfunction, includes gym
Management is lowkey annoying. Maintenance doesn't knock on room doors before entering.

Yugo Austin Waterloo.text: $35 a month green fee, great amenities (rooftop pool 30 floors high, gym, yoga room, saunas, cycling room, study area 2nd floor, free printing, Luxer package delivery system, refrigerators in mail room for grocery deliveries), however my first semester here we went down to 2 elevators out of the 4 in the building operational after just a week or two into the Fall semester. Being on the 25th floor made calling for an elevator extremely difficult with long wait times before seeing an elevator. By the time the elevator picked up people from floors 30-20 it was more or less full making people on lower floors have to wait even longer to get in an empty elevator. Additionally at times it would be down to 1 elevator because one of the elevators out of the 2 was getting overworked with the reduced elevator capacity making management slow down that elevator. Eventually they were fixed after 3 months (December) and have been fine ever since but definitely not a good elevator experience the first half of the year.

extremely tiny bedrooms but makes up for it with floor to ceiling windows, large kitchen island with waterfall countertop edge, and tower/campus view. decent amenities and aesthetic study spaces. elevator issues (often gets stuck/sometimes drop several floors). extremely tight parking garage!!!!!! (like every single car has scrapes down the side and it's pretty difficult to turn the corner without having to reverse)
Green fee, premium floor fee, they charge more if the trash room is overfilled even if it wasn't you. Thin walls
